subject: Sample Kit Exchange — Sprintcard & Acceptance Constraints
messages:
From: Elena Park <elena@orchard.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: Orchard.ai Legal <legal@orchard.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Orchard sample kit exchange & proposed sprintcard

Hi Hannah / Ben —

Thanks again for the product walkthrough last week. Orchard is ready to move into a short evaluation: we can share a 12k-example sample kit and a 20-case prompt pack to validate retrieval + reranking behavior against our customer data shapes.

Quick constraints from our side (legal asked me to flag these up front):
- Samples contain a small portion of customer PII (hashed) — must stay in a sandbox; no indexing outside the evaluation environment.
- Retention window: 30 days from ingest; then samples must be purged unless we agree otherwise.
- No model checkpoint export or model fine-tuning with our samples; obvious restriction but want it explicit.

I attached a preliminary manifest of the sample kit (orchard_sample_manifest.csv) and a draft sprintcard (MAP_sprintcard_v1.pdf) that lays out acceptance criteria (QA pass rates on 3 query buckets, latency targets, and token budget).

Proposed cadence:
- Day 0: NDA in place (we can provide our standard one) + ingress credentials to your sandbox.
- Day 1: Ingest and smoke tests.
- Day 3–7: MAP sprint (sample-driven eval).
- Day 10: Acceptance call to review results and next steps.

Let me know if those dates/constraints are workable and who on your side should own the operational checklist (ingest, masking verification, purge confirmation).

Thanks,
Elena
Head of ML Ops, Orchard.ai

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Park <elena@orchard.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>, Orchard.ai Legal <legal@orchard.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchard sample kit exchange & proposed sprintcard

Elena —

Appreciate the clear upfront constraints and the sprintcard doc. We can run this as a scoped MAP with the constraints you outlined. Summary of what we'll own and next steps below.

Operational owner: Ben Carter (sales/ops) will coordinate credentials and sandbox setup; engineering lead Priya Natarajan will take point on ingestion and masking verification with your team.

Key acceptance criteria we captured from MAP_sprintcard_v1.pdf (we'll reference these in the final MAP):
- Functional: 3 query buckets (freq, long-tail, adversarial) with >= 75% top-1 correctness on benchmark prompts.
- Performance: 95th percentile generation latency <= 450ms for the median token length in your manifest.
- Cost: token budget not to exceed 120k tokens during sprint window (we'll provide a token burn estimate ahead of Day 3).
- Security/compliance: samples restricted to a dedicated sandbox project with audit logging enabled; no model exports; purge policy enforced at T+30 days.

Questions / asks from our side:
1) Can Orchard provide an ingress service account with scoped IAM for the sandbox (S3 bucket + KMS key)?
2) For hashed PII, can you share the hash algorithm used (sha256 / salted?) so our masking verification step is deterministic?
3) We'll need a quick legal confirm on whether redlines to your NDA are expected; if so please route them to legal@redwood.ai.

Attachments: storing your manifest in our intake queue now. We'll draft a single-page MAP that ties the sprintcard acceptance criteria to deliverables and the timeline.

Proposed provisional timeline (we can tighten after we align on ingress and NDA):
- Wed (Day 0): Execute NDA, provision credentials.
- Thu (Day 1): Ingest + smoke tests.
- Fri–Mon (Day 3–6): Sprint runs and monitoring.
- Tue (Day 7): Internal review; Wed (Day 8): Joint acceptance call.

Ben / Priya: can you confirm resource availability for the Thu ingest window?

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference
[signature block]
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.ai>
Cc: Elena Park <elena@orchard.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 13:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Orchard sample kit exchange & proposed sprintcard

Hannah — quick operational note.

We can own Day 0 / Day 1 provisioning. Priya and I will be available for the ingest window on Thu. A few implementation notes so Orchard can prepare:
- Sandbox: we'll create a dedicated VPC project and an ephemeral bucket with lifecycle rules to enforce purge. We'll share a one-time KMS key binding and a service account for upload.
- Model variants: for the sprint we recommend using our canary variant (gptx-lite-1) to keep token spend low; we'll map acceptance tests to the production flavor only after acceptance.
- Logging: we'll enable audit logs + token-level usage CSV export for your verification team.

Operational asks for Orchard:
- Confirm the hash algorithm for PII (Hannah flagged it).
- Confirm max single-file size in the sample manifest (we prefer <= 5MB objects for fast ingestion).

I'll attach a short ops checklist after this thread (attachment stub).

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks — all sounds good from our side.

Answers:
- Hashing: we use salted sha256 (salt per-customer). We'll send a short note to legal with hashing details (copying Orchard.ai Legal).
- File size: we confirm <= 5MB per file; manifest has the file list.
- NDA: attached is our signed NDA (nda_signed_orchard.pdf). If Redwood wants to propose redlines, please send them to legal@orchard.ai.

We've signed and attached the NDA and are ready for Day 0 when you are. Also included is a DocuSign link in case you want a routed signature path for the MAP one-pager.

Next steps:
- Ben: please send the ephemeral S3 bucket + service account details and I will validate ingestion on Day 1.
- Priya: happy to sync on masking verification; I'll drop a short checklist into the shared drive (link below).
- Hannah: once you have a MAP one-pager, please circulate a calendar invite for the acceptance call.
